description.value: The study examined associations between attentional bias for smoking cues and brain responses to smoking cues among smokers with different DAT genotypes.

spans.text: The aim of the present study was to examine the associations between attentional bias for SCs and brain responses to SCs among 9-repeat and 10/10-repeat smokers.

description.value: Thirty-five physically healthy smokers were genotyped for the SLC6A3 polymorphism and underwent perfusion fMRI and attentional-bias testing.

definition.value: Brain perfusion during smoking cue exposure relative to non-smoking cue exposure in all smokers

spans.text: Brain perfusion during smoking cue exposure relative to non-smoking cue exposure

For each subject, a relative attentional bias score was computed as RT non-smoking – RT smoking ( Lubman et al., 2000 ) with positive bias scores reflecting attentional bias for SCs and negative scores reflecting bias towards nonsmoking cues.

Correlations between brain responses to SCs and attentional bias scores were computed for all subjects and then for each DAT genotype group by performing a regression analysis on ROI contrast images of interest (SCs versus non-SCs), using attentional bias scores as the dependent variable.

value: For the full sample of sated smokers, ROI analyses revealed significant activation to smoking cues relative to non-smoking cues in the medial orbitofrontal cortex and ventral striatum.

spans.text: For the full sample of sated smokers, ROI analyses revealed significant activation to SCs relative to non-SCs in the mOFC and VS.
